name: Banking system stress
summary: Financial stress gauges low; searches on 9 Nov found no notable bank failure or rescue
state: The St Louis Fed Financial Stress Index was −0.52 in the week to 30 Oct, below its long-run average, and the ECB's systemic stress indicator was 0.0068 on 5 Nov, far below the 0.25 Watch line (FRED; ECB). Searches on 9 Nov found no mid-sized or larger bank failure or rescue in the US or Europe; the FDIC's list shows only small failures this year.
for_you: Bank deposits are covered up to set limits by national guarantee schemes, in the UK the FSCS. Current readings show no sign of system-wide strain.
rubric_hit: STLFSI -0.52 below the 0 Watch line; ECB CISS 0.01 below the 0.25 Watch line

sources.title: FRED — St Louis Fed Financial Stress Index
American Banker — Most recent bank failures

why: Bank failures turn market losses into credit crunches; 2008 and 2023 both began as 'contained' bank problems.
drivers: Rate shocks to bond portfolios, commercial property losses, deposit flight, private-credit links.

rubric.alert: STLFSI > 1.5, or ECB CISS > 0.45, or a systemically important bank fails or needs rescue, or emergency central-bank facilities launched.
rubric.watch: STLFSI 0–1.5, or ECB CISS 0.25–0.45, or a mid-sized bank failure/rescue, or a large bank under visible funding pressure.
rubric.normal: St Louis Fed Financial Stress Index < 0, ECB CISS < 0.25, and no notable bank failures or rescues.
